documents_checked.document_title: Copyright advice for teaching research and students
documents_checked.text:
All teaching and learning materials are copyright protected ‘works’. This includes not just book
chapters and journal articles, film, television and other audio-visual content, but everything
else as well: unit study guides, lecture notes,
quizzes and exam questions, slide presentations and the text and images used in them,
recorded lectures, etc. None of these works should be passed on or sold outside the University,
either online or in print.
Murdoch University staff and students are expected to comply with the Copyright Act 1968
(Cth), and with both the University Copyright Policy and Intellectual Property Regulations.

case_summary.case_note: Murdoch's Privacy Policy (N083) regulates University collection of personal and biometric data, while Copyright advice (N235) and myAccess guidance (N233) address recorded lectures and assistive technology generally. No relevant provision was identified in the documents and searches checked establishing a permission or consent boundary for a student's undisclosed AI assistant recording live lecture participants, leaving a critical gap. Protocol v1.1 was adopted after preliminary review on 2026-11-15, and this proposal awaits human verification.
